Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Senator [[Jacky Rosen]] narrowly won re-election to a second term, defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee [[Sam Brown (military officer)|Sam Brown]].{{cite news |url=https://apnews.com/article/nevada-senate-election-race-2024-f6646cfc6bdfb00d78897322cd25ae44 |title=Democratic US Sen. Jacky Rosen is reelected in Nevada, securing battleground seat |first1=Nicholas |last1=Riccardi |first2=Rio |last2=Yamat |publisher=Associated Press |date=November 9, 2024 |access-date=November 9, 2024}} Republican presidential nominee [[Donald Trump]] carried Nevada on the [[2024 United States presidential election in Nevada|same ballot]]. Primary elections took place on June 11, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-08-06 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Incumbent Democratic senator Jacky Rosen was running for reelection to a second term in office, facing a strong challenge from Republican author and [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] veteran Sam Brown. Brown was endorsed by [[Donald Trump]], who was running for the presidency up the ballot. Given Nevada's status as a crucial [[Swing state|swing state]] at the federal level, a competitive race was anticipated; although, Rosen led most all of preelection polling, and almost all major news organizations and firms predicted that she was likely to win, albeit by varying levels of confidence. Come Election Day, Rosen was reelected by a narrow margin of around 1.7%, an advantage of around 24,000 votes among over 1.46 million cast statewide. This result reflected a somewhat more competitive result than expected, according to final polling averages, and was down from her [[2018 United States Senate election in Nevada|2018]] margin of around 5 points against then-incumbent Republican senator [[Dean Heller]]. Rosen received 47.9% of the statewide vote to Brown's 46.2%. Rosen's victory came on the same ballot in which Democrat [[Kamala Harris]] lost the state of Nevada in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Nevada|concurrent presidential election]] by 3.1%, becoming the first Democrat to do so since [[2004 United States presidential election in Nevada|2004]]. To compare to the presidential race, Rosen ultimately overperformed Harris by around 4.8 percentage points. Rosen carried two of Nevada's seventeen [[List of counties in Nevada|counties]] – [[Clark County, Nevada|Clark County]], home to [[Las Vegas]] and [[Las Vegas Valley|its suburbs]], and [[Washoe County, Nevada|Washoe County]], home to [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]] and [[Reno metropolitan area|its suburbs]] – which is somewhat of a traditional result in the state, as Harris did the same in the presidential election; however, their margins differed notably. Rosen carried Clark and Washoe counties by margins of 7.3% and 5.8% respectively, while Harris only carried them by 2.6% and 1.0% respectively. Rosen received around 4,000 fewer votes than Harris, while Brown received over 74,000 fewer votes than Trump. ==Background== A typical swing state, Nevada is considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|purple]] state at the federal level, especially since in the [[2016 United States presidential election]], when [[Hillary Clinton]] carried Nevada by about two percentage points. Both parties have seen success in the state in recent years. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] control both [[U.S. Senate]] seats, majorities in both state legislative chambers, and all but one seat in its congressional delegation, while [[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] flipped the governorship and lieutenant governorship in [[2022 Nevada gubernatorial election|2022]].{{Cite web |last=Edelman |first=Adam |date=November 11, 2022 |title=Republican Joe Lombardo has won the race for governor in Nevada, defeating Democratic incumbent Steve Sisolak |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/republican-joe-lombardo-won-race-governor-nevada-defeating-democratic-rcna55514 |access-date=2023-03-14 |website=NBC News |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Sonner |first=Scott |date=November 11, 2022 |title=Nevada Democrats Sweep 3 Key House Seats in Close Battles |url=https://www.usnews.com/news/politics/articles/2022-11-11/rep-dina-titus-holds-democratic-stronghold-in-las-vegas |access-date=March 14, 2022 |website=en}}{{Cite news |last=Anguiano |first=Dani |date=2022-11-13 |title=Catherine Cortez Masto wins Nevada Senate race to hold Democratic seat |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/nov/13/catherine-cortez-masto-wins-nevada-senate-race |access-date=2023-03-14 |issn=0261-3077}} As of 2024, no [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] has won any [[U.S. Senate]] race in [[Nevada]] since 2012.
